tier: a-la-carte 1 vCPU / 2 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk (the beefiest shape under USD 5 at 730 h)

free_tier.stated: Claim $5 in free credit - one-time, per account, and nothing is charged for it. Signing up is free and takes no payment details.
free_tier.notes: credit, not hours: USD 5 of prepaid balance

retention.stated: Power off a Cube and its disk is kept exactly as you left it; only the disk keeps billing, at USD 0.00005/GB/hour on the full provisioned size.

egress.terms: Unmetered. Krova does not bill per gigabyte and sets no monthly transfer allowance; the network is shared and sustained heavy traffic can be rate-limited. Outbound TCP 25 is blocked.

interface_detail: Root SSH on a per-Cube hostname and port, a REST API with API keys, and a dashboard. 'You log in as ubuntu ... Run sudo su for a root shell.'
tooling: any SSH client; rsync/scp over the SSH mapping; the REST API for create/start/stop; no vendor rclone backend needed because it is a plain Linux box
chaining: A USD 2.92 a month always-on Linux box with root, unmetered egress and no card at signup: the cheapest credible always-on target, usable as a monitor, a small web app behind Krova's HTTPS proxy, or a Docker host, but not as a WireGuard endpoint because only TCP can be published.

limits.value: no UDP ingress and no public IPv4: services are exposed as on-demand TCP port mappings with an optional allowlist, or through Krova's HTTPS proxy
outbound TCP port 25 blocked on every Cube; other ports open

limits_note: Two hard limits that the seven-kind vocabulary cannot name. (1) There is no public IPv4 and no UDP ingress: 'Outbound: everything. Inbound: your call' is implemented as on-demand TCP port mappings with IP allowlists plus an HTTPS proxy for web traffic, so a WireGuard or QUIC listener cannot be reached from outside. (2) Concurrency is tiered: 3 Cubes running at once on Welcome, 10 after USD 15 of lifetime top-ups, 25 after USD 50, uncapped after USD 300. Cube size is the same on every tier: up to 16 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 100 GB disk.
binding_note: What fails first is not one of the seven kinds: there is no UDP ingress and no public IPv4, so a WireGuard or QUIC listener cannot be reached. Recorded in limits[] as per-ip-shaping with the protocol limit spelled out rather than mislabelled as a quota.

identity_cost.detail: Email link or 6-digit code, or Google; 'No credit card to sign up'. The USD 5 credit is granted at account activation with nothing charged, and the Welcome tier unlocks with it, so a card is needed only to top up (one-time Stripe Checkout) or to enable auto-recharge. No hold is stated. Debit acceptance is not stated.

reliability_note: domain registered 2026-03-14; prepaid credit is not refundable in cash; the disk is deleted 7 days after the balance reaches zero

identity, resolved: 'Top up from Billing with a card (one-time, via Stripe Checkout). Activating your account credits you $5 to start (one-time, per account) and unlocks the Welcome tier automatically — nothing is charged for it.'

notes: The nearest published preset, Micro at 1 / 2 / 20, is USD 5.11 and therefore over the line. 15 GiB of disk instead of 10 would be USD 4.93. Its credit is non-refundable in cash and its disk is deleted seven days after the balance hits zero, so it is a prepaid bet rather than a subscription. The domain is seven months old. Against that: a status page on UptimeRobot reports 99.996%, which is better evidence than most hosts in this price band publish.

extras.price_arithmetic: 730 h x (1 x 0.0010 + 2 x 0.0025 + 10 x 0.00005) = 730 x 0.0065 = USD 4.745. 10 h/day = 300 x 0.0065 = USD 1.95. The published 1/1/10 preset is 730 x 0.004 = USD 2.92; the published 1/2/20 preset is 730 x 0.007 = USD 5.11. Powered off, only disk bills: 10 GB x 0.00005 x 730 = USD 0.365 a month.

network_out.ports: TCP only, via on-demand port mappings with an optional IP allowlist; no public IPv4 and no UDP; HTTPS through Krova's proxy for custom domains

session_cap.note: no lifetime cap; it is an always-on microVM

extras.aggregator_note: sandboxprices.com models 0.25 vCPU / 0.47 GiB / 4.66 GiB at 200 active hours and rounds up to this 1 vCPU / 1 GB / 10 GB preset; its USD 1.065 is not the 24/7 price of the machine, which is USD 2.92.
